item: Overlapping flushes of the vitals history file can no longer tear it: one flush at a time
summary: The budget test of the heaviest vitals member failed once on #1381 in a job that crossed midnight UTC (15 fine rows where 577 had been written). Not the date: frozen-clock runs around midnight, new year and a leap day give the same member. flush() wrote and renamed vitals_history.json.tmp under one fixed name, so two overlapping flushes (the liveness thread's, the clean stop's, the exit flush, a thread a test left running) tore the file, and start() read it as none and began an empty history (28 of 150 builds lost it; 0 of 150 with the lock). _FLUSH_LOCK (an RLock) is now held for the whole flush: the _STARTED re-check in the same hold as the snapshot, the write, os.replace and the bookkeeping; order _FLUSH_LOCK, _LOCK, _LOG_LOCK. Not covered, and said so: a nested flush on one thread, two processes on one directory. The member's method text and the _gaps docstring say, as three cases, that a recorded clock step can leave its gap unmarked. Tests read the file DURING the overlap (5 to 21 of 300 loads torn without the lock; skipped on Windows), a flush that waited across a reset writes nothing, the member built a second either side of midnight is the same, and the isolation-fixture guard reads the fixture from the syntax tree. One independent read (0 block, 0 should-fix, 9 low) folded; the coordinator's check OK; ruff advisory 417 of 417.
